bikrampur-atish-dipankar.desc: Atish Dipankar Srijnan was born in Bikrampur, traditionally at Bajrayogini near Munshiganj, in the late 10th century. He taught at Vikramashila and travelled to Tibet, where he is still revered as a key teacher. Bajrayogini has a memorial at the site associated with his birthplace, and Buddhist visitors from abroad sometimes come on pilgrimage. Together with Nateshwar, it shows how important Bikrampur once was as a centre of learning.

arial-beel.desc: Arial Beel is a large, low-lying wetland between the Padma and Dhaleshwari, much of it in Sreenagar upazila. In monsoon and early autumn it fills with water and white and red shapla lilies, and small boats glide between village islands. In the dry season the land is farmed, and the beel is known for very large sweet pumpkins. It is one of the closest real wetland landscapes to Dhaka.
blocks: How to get there
From Dhaka take the Mawa expressway to Sreenagar, then a local auto and boat into the beel.
Good to know
Go early morning for lilies; hire a boat locally and carry sun protection.

glance: 42 km to Munshiganj by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
idrakpur-fort.desc: Idrakpur Fort was built around 1660 under Mir Jumla, the Mughal governor of Bengal, to guard the rivers against pirate raids. Its most memorable feature is a high circular platform where cannon once stood, linked to the main enclosure by a ramp. The walls are crenellated and the brickwork has been restored. It takes less than an hour to explore and is right in town.
blocks: How to get there
Bus or launch from Dhaka to Munshiganj town, then a rickshaw to the fort.
Good to know
Combine with a launch trip on the Dhaleshwari for a full day out.

jc-bose-complex-rarikhal.desc: Rarikhal village in Sreenagar was the ancestral home of the scientist Jagadish Chandra Bose. His family estate of about 30 acres, with old ponds and trees, now holds the J.C. Bose Institution (a school founded in 1921) and a memorial complex built around 2011. The small museum shows his portrait, photographs and copies of letters and papers, and the grounds have fountains, a pond ghat and murals. Visitors have found the museum modest and not always well kept, but the leafy estate is a pleasant stop on a Bikrampur trip.
blocks: How to get there
From Dhaka take a bus on the Dhaka–Mawa expressway to Sreenagar, then a CNG or auto to Rarikhal.
Good to know
Check museum hours locally before going. Combine it with Bhagyakul or the Padma at Mawa on the same day.

glance: 42 km to Munshiganj by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
nateshwar-buddhist-site.desc: Excavations since around 2013 at Nateshwar in Tongibari upazila have uncovered brick stupas, temple platforms and other structures from Bikrampur's Buddhist period, roughly a thousand years ago. The site supports the region's link with Atish Dipankar, the scholar born in Bikrampur who carried Buddhist teaching to Tibet. Parts of the excavation are open to visitors, with paths along the trenches. Few tourists come, so you may have it largely to yourself.
blocks: How to get there
CNG from Munshiganj town to Tongibari, then a local auto to Nateshwar.
Good to know
Stay on paths and do not climb on exposed brickwork.

glance: 42 km to Munshiganj by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
baba-adam-mosque.desc: Baba Adam's Mosque stands in Qazi Qasba village of Rampal, the old heart of Bikrampur. An inscription over the central door dates it to 1483, in the reign of Sultan Jalaluddin Fath Shah, and names its builder as the officer Malik Kafur. The brick prayer hall is roofed by six equal domes in two rows, carried on slender octagonal black basalt pillars and the doorways and mihrabs sit in recessed rectangular frames. The tomb of Baba Adam Shahid, a 15th-century preacher, lies close by. It is a protected monument and is still used for prayer.
blocks: How to get there
From Munshiganj town take a rickshaw or auto to Rampal (Qazi Qasba), about 3–4 km away.
Good to know
Avoid prayer times and dress modestly. Pair it with the Rampal dighi and Ballal Bari area nearby for a Bikrampur heritage morning.

glance: Sweet shops in Bhagyakul bazar, Sreenagar
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
bhagyakul-mishti.desc: Bhagyakul, a river village in Sreenagar upazila, has a long reputation for sweets made with good local milk. Rasgolla, sandesh and doi are the classics, softer and less sugary than many factory sweets. Shops using the Bhagyakul name have spread to Dhaka, but locals say the best are still found at home. Pick up a box on the way to or from Mawa.

mawa-padma-riverside.desc: Mawa on the north bank of the Padma was for decades the busiest ferry ghat on the route to the south-west. The Padma Bridge, opened in 2022, now crosses the river close by, and its roughly 6 km span is an impressive sight from the bank. Boatmen offer trips out on the river, and the old ghat area still has rows of hilsa restaurants. Sunset over the Padma here is worth staying for.
blocks: How to get there
Bus via the Dhaka–Mawa expressway, about 1 hour from Dhaka.
Good to know
Stopping on the bridge itself is not allowed; view it from the riverbank or a boat.

glance: Priced per piece or per fish; ask first
mawa-ilish-bhaja.desc: The ghat restaurants of Mawa became famous for frying hilsa fresh from the Padma. You pick your fish, it is cut into steaks and fried crisp, then served with steaming rice, fried roe, chopped onion and green chilli. Many places also serve begun bhaja and dal alongside. Since the bridge opened, many Dhaka residents drive down just for this meal.

glance: Sweet makers and bazaars of Sirajdikhan, and sweet shops in Munshiganj town

munshiganj-patkhir.desc: Patkhir is milk boiled down slowly until it turns into a dense, mildly sweet khir, traditionally set in shallow pots lined with leaves. Sirajdikhan upazila is the best-known home of it, and Munshiganj's patkhir received Geographical Indication status in 2025. In winter it is the classic filling for patishapta pitha; in summer people eat it with ripe mango, milk and muri. Some locals like it plain in the morning with strong red tea.

glance: Shree Durga Mistanna Bhandar in Haldia bazar, Louhajang, about 10–15 minutes from the old Mawa ghat
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
louhajang-rosogolla.desc: Louhajang, on the old road to Mawa, is sometimes called the sweet capital of greater Dhaka. Its rosogolla is made with thick milk from local cattle, so it comes out tender and milky rather than spongy. Halwai families here have passed the craft down for generations, and Muslim sweet makers trained by them have spread it further. Shree Durga Mistanna Bhandar, a tin-roofed shop in Haldia bazar run by Ganesh Ghosh and his son, serves it hot straight from the pan.

glance: 42 km to Munshiganj by road, 1–2 hours by bus or car
sonarang-twin-temples.desc: The Sonarang jora math are two tall Hindu temples standing next to each other beside a pond in Tongibari upazila. Built in the 19th century, the taller tower rises high above the surrounding trees and is visible from a distance. The weathered brick and plaster give them a dramatic, slightly eerie look. It is a short detour from Munshiganj town and pairs well with the Buddhist sites nearby.
blocks: How to get there
CNG from Munshiganj town to Tongibari, then ask for Sonarang.
